bib.title: Extending Context Window of Large Language Models via Position Interpolation

question: Can the context window of an existing pretrained RoPE LLM be extended cheaply without extrapolating to unseen positions?
hypothesis: Interpolating position indices into the trained range is easier for the model to adapt to than extrapolating.
contributions: PI extends LLaMA 7B to 65B to up to 32768 with at most 1000 fine-tuning steps
Extended models use longer windows for language modeling (perplexity falls)
Quality preserved relatively well within the original window
Theoretical interpolation bound ~600x smaller than extrapolation bound

method.summary: Position Interpolation rescales RoPE position indices from [0, L') to [0, L) (f'(x,m)=f(x, mL/L')) so a longer input sits inside the trained position range, then fine-tunes briefly with next-token prediction. LLaMA 7B to 65B extended to 8192, 16384 and 32768 and evaluated on perplexity, passkey retrieval, original benchmarks and GovReport summarisation.
method.task: context window extension of pretrained RoPE LLMs

datasets.name: Arxiv Math Proof-pile
datasets.size: 128 random documents with at least 32768 SentencePiece tokens

datasets.name: GovReport
datasets.preprocessing: inputs truncated to first 15000 tokens; ground-truth summary truncated to 1000 tokens; prompt-part loss excluded

datasets.name: Passkey retrieval (synthetic)
datasets.size: 32 values of k x 10 runs per model

datasets.name: LLaMA benchmarks BoolQ PIQA Race-M Race-H WinoGrande

training.objective: next token prediction with interpolated position encodings
training.warmup: linear warmup 20 steps starting from 10% of max lr
training.batch_size: 64 global (7B/13B/33B to 8192, 32 A100); 128 global otherwise (128 A100)
training.steps: 1000 for PI unless specified; 10000 for direct fine-tuning; GovReport fine-tune 10 epochs
training.hardware: 32 or 128 A100 GPUs; PyTorch, FSDP, Flash Attention

other.note: PI step count is 1000 by default; Table 3/4 report 200 to 1000 steps

inference.samples: passkey: 10 runs per k; perplexity and benchmarks single run

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: sliding-window, stride 256, at various context sizes

metrics.name: kmax (effective context window)
metrics.definition: max k such that for all k' <= k success rate on passkey at distance k' is at least 20%

eval.protocol: single run per configuration; no seeds or significance tests stated

availability.code: appendix C code for Fig 2 and Fig 5 only

Summary:

evidence.quote: kmax is defined as the maximum k such that, for all k′ ≤k, the model has a success rate of at least 20% on k′.

results.claim: Direct extrapolation of a RoPE LLaMA 7B past its 2048 training window gives perplexity above 1000 at 4096 to 32768.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B, trained at 2048, PG19 test (100 docs), sliding window stride 256
results.quote: the perplexity may shoot up to very high numbers (i.e., > 103), comparable to untrained models.

results.claim: With PI and no fine-tuning, 7B extended to 8192 has PG19 perplexity under 20; 16384 gives 112.13 at step 0.
results.quote: as indicated by < 20 perplexity for extending to 8192 context window

results.claim: After 200 PI fine-tuning steps the 7B models surpass the original model's 2048-window perplexity.
results.quote: At 200 steps the models surpassed the original model’s perplexity on 2048 context window size

results.claim: PI reaches effective window kmax = L' after 200 fine-tuning steps for 7B and 33B at 8192 and 16384 (7B 32768 also, except 18432 at 600 steps).
results.setup: Passkey retrieval, 32 values of k uniformly spaced in L', 10 runs each, 5-digit passkey; kmax = largest k such that all k' <= k have success rate >= 20%
results.note: Table 4 cell 7B 32768 PI at 600 steps is 18432, a dip below L'; the text does not comment on it.
results.quote: the effective context window size reaching maximum kmax = L′, after merely fine-tuning for 200 steps

results.claim: Direct fine-tuning raises effective window only from 2048 to 2560 after 10000 steps.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B extended to 8192 by direct fine-tuning, passkey kmax
results.quote: only saw a minimal increase of the effective context window size kmax from 2048 to 2560, even after fine-tuning for more than 10000 steps

results.claim: Extended 7B at 8192 raises PG19 perplexity gain with window: 7.13 at 2048 to 6.95 at 8192; direct FT gets worse (7.21 to 7.69).
results.setup: LLaMA 7B, PG19, PI vs FT, 8192 context

results.claim: Going from 2048 to 16384 reduces perplexity by 0.28 (PG19) and 0.5 (Proof-pile) for 7B.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B extended with PI, PG19 and Proof-pile
results.quote: By increasing the context window size from 2048 to 16384, we observed -0.28 and -0.5 reductions of perplexity for extending LLaMA 7B models on both datasets

results.claim: PI costs a small perplexity loss within the original 2048 window on Proof-pile.
results.quote: we saw a degradation ranging from 0.01 to 0.05 across all models with extended with Position Interpolation

results.claim: Models extended to 8192 lose up to 2% on short-context benchmarks; longer extensions regress more.
results.setup: LLaMA 7B and 33B, zero-shot BoolQ, PIQA, Race-M, Race-H, WinoGrande, within 2048 tokens
results.note: Table 5 shows 7B 8192 Pile BoolQ 73.2 vs 76.1 original, a 2.9 point drop (percent unit ambiguous: points vs relative). RedPajama fine-tune BoolQ 75.5. Text says 'up to 2%'; caption singles out BoolQ as the exception.
results.quote: with a degradation of up to 2% on the benchmark tasks, for both 7B and 33B model sizes

results.claim: 7B BoolQ falls from 76.1 to 64.7 at 32768 extension.
LLaMA-7B extended to 16K gets GovReport ROUGE-1 60.0, ROUGE-2 28.0, ROUGE-L 29.5, competitive on R1 with CoLT5 Base (58.7) and below CoLT5 XL (61.3).
results.setup: GovReport 17457 train / 972 eval docs, inputs truncated to 15000 tokens, 16384 window, 10 epochs fine-tune, temperature 0.5, top_p 0.95, output truncated at 1000 tokens
results.table: Table 6, row LLaMA-7B Extended, column ROUGE-1

results.claim: Theory: interpolation upper bound is at least ~600x smaller than extrapolation bound (LLaMA 7B setting, c=10000, d=128).
results.quote: the interpolation bound is at least 2 · 294.73 ∼600× smaller than the extrapolation bound

results.claim: Fine-tuning on Pile vs RedPajama made no significant benchmark difference.
results.quote: the choice of fine-tuning datasets does not seem to lead significant difference in the benchmark performances

limits: Evaluates only LLaMA (RoPE); applicability to other encodings is conjecture
Effective window measured on passkey retrieval only, with a 20% success threshold
Perplexity degrades slightly in the original window; BoolQ degrades markedly at 32768 (64.7 vs 76.1)
Only one run per configuration; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated
65B only extended to 8192; 33B to 16384; 32768 only for 7B and 13B
Summarisation compared only against CoLT5 on one dataset
Authors suggest regularising |h_j| during pretraining as untested future work
Pile token count of fine-tuning not stated; steps x batch size 128 x seq len is implied only
